case.label: D
case.text: A gateway VPC endpoint for Amazon S3 has no hourly or per-GB charge and removes the NAT gateway data processing for the EC2 uploads, so on cost alone it beats A; a candidate who reads 'reduce the NAT gateway data processing charges' as the main goal and treats the data center sentence as background would pick it. The case fails because the stem makes on-premises traffic a hard requirement ('All uploads must reach Amazon S3 privately through the VPC', with the data center connected over a Direct Connect private virtual interface), and a gateway endpoint is reached only through VPC route tables, so the data center servers cannot use it; the cheaper mixed design (gateway endpoint for EC2 plus interface endpoint for on-premises) is not offered, so A is the cheapest option that meets every requirement. C also meets the requirements but adds a second NAT gateway, which only raises cost. Wording cues: A and C share the phrase 'interface VPC endpoint ... in each Availability Zone', and A is the most specific option, which can point a test-wise candidate to A without reading the Direct Connect constraint; this is a mild cue, not a second answer.
